strategy.summary: GET /products (src/app.js listProducts) filters the in-memory catalogue by case-insensitive name substring `q`, pages with `limit` (default 20, capped at MAX_LIMIT = 50) and `offset` (default 0), returns `{ total, items }`, and refuses non-whole-number limit/offset or limit < 1 with 400. Integration tests start the real app in-process on port 0 and call it with fetch, proving filtering, paging, total, capping and refusals.
inScope: GET /products query parameters q, limit, offset
Response shape { total, items } and 400 refusals
outOfScope: GET /products/:id and POST /orders (not part of this ticket)
Updating the stale README limit (docs, not tests)
assumptions: The cap is MAX_LIMIT = 50 as in src/app.js; the README's 'up to 100' is stale (confirmed by a person in earlier runs on this ticket). Tests import MAX_LIMIT and DEFAULT_LIMIT rather than hard-coding them.
The app runs for real in-process (createApp().listen(0)); nothing is faked. The catalogue is the fixed 120-product list in src/catalogue.js, which GET /products only reads, so tests share it safely.
Server start/stop moves into a shared helper test/helpers/server.js used by both test/products.test.js and the new spec, instead of copying the setup.
Results come in catalogue (id) order, as the code filters PRODUCTS in place.
openQuestions: README.md says limit goes up to 100 while the code caps at 50; README should be updated (follow-up).

risks.description: Search is case-sensitive or matches only prefixes, so the shop search misses products
risks.mitigation: TC1 uses a mixed-case query matching mid-name and asserts exact total and names

risks.description: total reports page size instead of all matches, breaking pagination UI
risks.mitigation: TC4/TC5/TC7 assert total differs from page length

risks.description: Uncapped limit lets clients dump the whole catalogue
risks.mitigation: TC6 asks for MAX_LIMIT+1 and asserts exactly MAX_LIMIT items

risks.description: Bad paging input gives 200 with odd slices instead of 400
risks.mitigation: TC9-TC11 check each malformed value and limit=0

acceptanceCriteria.text: `q` returns products whose name contains it case-insensitively; without `q` every product is listed.
Results are paged by `limit` and `offset`, the response's `total` is the number of all matches, and limits above MAX_LIMIT are capped to MAX_LIMIT.
A `limit` or `offset` that isn't a whole number, or a `limit` below 1, is refused with 400.

testCases.title: matches names containing q in any case
testCases.expected: 200; total 30; items are exactly the Teapot and Tea strainer products (30 items, each name contains 'tea' ignoring case, first 'Teapot 1', 'Tea strainer 1')

testCases.title: lists every product when q is absent
testCases.expected: 200; total equals PRODUCTS.length (120); items are the first DEFAULT_LIMIT products by id

testCases.title: returns no items and a total of 0 when nothing matches q
testCases.rationale: Search must not fall back to listing all

testCases.title: returns the page selected by limit and offset with the total of all matches
returns no items but the full total when offset is past the last match
caps a limit above MAX_LIMIT to MAX_LIMIT items
accepts the smallest limit of 1
testCases.expected: 200; items is exactly product id 1; total 120
testCases.rationale: Accepted side of the limit>=1 boundary

testCases.title: refuses a limit of 0 with 400
testCases.expected: 400 with a JSON body containing an error string

testCases.title: refuses limit=$value with 400 because it isn't a whole number
testCases.expected: 400 with a JSON error string for each

testCases.title: refuses offset=$value with 400 because it isn't a whole number
testCases.expected: 400 with a JSON error string for each

strategy.environmentNotes: No external services; the app runs in-process on an OS-chosen port via test/helpers/server.js. Runs under the existing `npm test` (vitest run).
